title: bug: the JetBrains plugin reads MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND only when no bundled daemon script resolves, so the override is dead in a normal install. For the documented example `npx moe-daemon` it never appends `start`, so when the override is used it runs `npx moe-daemon --project <path>`, which prints usage and exits 0 without starting a daemon
description:
Hunt #17 (task-3488566e) found this as held item (b). The governor re-checked the code at 59e95024.

- **Spawn order:** MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:182-190 uses buildDirectDaemonCommand (the bundled or local daemon script) whenever that script resolves. It falls back to buildDaemonCommand, the only reader of MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND, only when the script does not resolve. Yet docs/CONFIGURATION.md:60 documents MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND as the "Daemon start command override (JetBrains plugin)", and CLAUDE.md describes it as override resolution.
- **Missing `start`:** buildDaemonCommand (:665-690) appends `start` only when the command ends in .cmd, .ps1 or .js, or equals `moe-daemon`. So the documented example `npx moe-daemon` becomes `npx moe-daemon --project "<path>"`. Given no subcommand, the daemon CLI prints usage and exits 0 without writing daemon.json. Evidence: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/A/repro-daemon-command.{sh,out}.
- **WSL host suffix:** the override branch returns before the WSL agent-mode `--host` suffix is added. Check whether an override daemon in WSL agent mode binds loopback only.

Fix direction:
- An explicitly set MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND wins over the bundled script.
- Append `start` whenever the command names no daemon subcommand. Match the daemon CLI's subcommand list, not file extensions.
- In WSL agent mode, add the same --host suffix as the other spawn paths unless the command already carries --host.
- Keep the {projectPath} template and an explicit --project working as they do today.

Placement: task-fe811130 also edits MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt (the bindHost probe). Edit only buildDaemonCommand and the spawn-path selection, and put the tests in their own test class or block. No dependency edge is needed in worktree mode. The Kotlin gate is gradlew.bat test from Windows, run under the jetbrains-gradle lease.
definitionOfDone: With MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND set, the plugin spawns the override even when a bundled daemon script resolves. With it unset, the spawn path is unchanged. A JUnit test pins both cases.

buildDaemonCommand turns `npx moe-daemon`, or any command that names no daemon subcommand, into one that runs `start --project <path>`. It leaves unchanged a command that already names a subcommand, carries --project or uses {projectPath}. In WSL agent mode it adds the --host suffix the other spawn paths add, unless the command already carries --host. JUnit tests pin each case.
docs/CONFIGURATION.md's MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND row states the precedence and the start rule. `./gradlew test` passes, run as gradlew.bat test from Windows under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

implementationPlan.description:
DOCS (the CONFIGURATION.md half of DoD 3): edit docs/CONFIGURATION.md with the session's own editing tool: Edit on a Claude seat, apply_patch on a codex exec seat, never Serena or a shell write. Replace only the `MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND` row (:60, Agent Scripts table), keeping its four columns.
- Description. It must state: the JetBrains plugin's daemon start command; when set (non-blank) it wins over every daemon script the plugin finds (the bundled, repository or global-config copy); the protected profile never reads it and starts only the installed daemon; the plugin runs it with `bash -lc` (`cmd /c` on Windows) after these rewrites: `{projectPath}` becomes the project path, and a command that carries `--project` or `{projectPath}` is otherwise used as written; any other command gets `start` appended unless it already names a daemon subcommand (`start`, `stop`, `status`, `init`, `doctor`, `version`, `accounts`, `check-architecture`, `_run`), then `--project "<path>"`; the daemon reads its subcommand only as its first argument, so a command with arguments of its own must name it (`npx moe-daemon start --port 9877`); in WSL agent mode `--host wsl` is appended unless the command carries `--host`; the Windows installer sets it to its `start-daemon.cmd` shim, so an installer machine starts that daemon instead of the bundled one.
- Default column: `Unset (bundled daemon)`. Example column: `npx moe-daemon`, unchanged.
Touch no other line. docs/PLUGIN_SPEC.md:74, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:63 and installer/README.md:37 already agree with the new precedence. CONFIGURATION.md is not vendored into the daemon's generated files, so nothing needs regenerating.
implementationPlan.note: Replaced only the MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND row: precedence, start rule, --project/{projectPath}, WSL --host rule, installer note; default column now "Unset (bundled daemon)".

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the legacy profile, a non-blank MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND is the daemon start command even when a bundled, repository or global-config daemon script resolves; an unset, blank or unreadable one keeps today's direct spawn. The override is rewritten so that it starts a daemon: `start` is appended when it names no daemon subcommand and carries neither --project nor {projectPath}; `--project "<path>"` is appended as before; and in WSL agent mode `--host wsl` is appended unless it carries --host. The protected profile never reads it.
acceptanceCriteria: With an override set and a resolving daemon script, the spawned command is the shell (`bash -lc`, or `cmd /c` on Windows) running the rewritten override.
`npx moe-daemon` becomes `npx moe-daemon start --project "<path>"`, and a command naming a subcommand gets no second `start`.
A command carrying --project or {projectPath} is used as written, apart from the template substitution and the WSL --host suffix.
In WSL agent mode the override command carries exactly one --host.
invariants: PROTECTED never calls daemonCommandOverride and still spawns only the installed daemon.
With no override, the spawn command is identical to before: the direct script, the installed start-daemon.cmd, or the moe-daemon fallback.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Keep System.getenv inside buildDaemonCommand and Assume-skip in tests (today's W2): no override case could be pinned, because a JVM cannot set its own environment; a constructor seam like the file's other seams is used instead. 2) Insert `start` right after the daemon program: the program's end cannot be found in a shell string (`npx -y moe-daemon`, `node --flag index.js`), so `start` is only appended, and the docs say a command with its own arguments must name the subcommand. 3) Append `start` to commands carrying --project or {projectPath}: the daemon reads its subcommand only as its first argument (index.ts parseArgs), so an appended start cannot fix them, and the DoD keeps them as written. 4) Clear MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND for the test JVM in build.gradle.kts: a build-file edit for two tests; injecting `{ null }` into W1/W2 stays local. 5) Constants in the companion object: kept as private members next to buildDaemonCommand instead, away from the companion, where task-fe811130 is likely to add bindHost constants. DoD reading: 'leaves unchanged a command that already names a subcommand' means no `start` is inserted; `--project "<path>"` is still appended as today.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Spawn order today (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:182-196): PROTECTED uses the installed daemon only. LEGACY uses buildDirectDaemonCommand (repo packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js, moe-daemon/dist/index.js, the bundled daemon/index.js, the global-config copy). Only when none resolves does it take the shell command from buildDaemonCommand, the only reader of MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND.
- Daemon CLI (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts): parseArgs takes `args[0] || 'start'`. main() handles accounts before parseArgs. The word cases are start, stop, status, init, doctor, check-architecture, version and _run. Anything else prints usage and exits 0, which is the bug's symptom.
- installer/moe-installer.iss:20 sets MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND to the quoted path of its start-daemon.cmd shim, which runs `node index.js %*`. Today the override is dead there, because the bundled daemon always resolves.
- RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt:2243 constructs the supervisor with 11 positional args, so the seam must sit after processLookup.
- MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.FakeProcess is private. W2 (:524) is the only existing reference to the variable, and its comment becomes false with this fix.
- The Windows gate host's environment has no MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND (checked 2026-11-04), so the existing suite is unaffected there; W1/W2 get `{ null }` anyway.
planningNotes.risks:
- Windows installer machines change behaviour: the installer's MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND now wins, so the plugin starts the installer's daemon instead of its bundled one. DoD 1 intends this, and the docs row says so. The bundled-docs upgrade still runs before the spawn, and the daemon rewrites stale marked copies at its own start.
- Under `bash -lc`, a `$` or backtick in a project path still expands inside `--project "<path>"`, unchanged from today.
- `--project` detection stays today's substring check. Subcommand and `--host` detection are word matches, so a flag value equal to a subcommand (`--name init`) suppresses `start`.
- task-fe811130 edits the same file. The hunks are placed apart (step 1), but on a landing conflict keep both sides.
- Gradle runs are your own processes: hold the lease only around them and release it on failure too.

completionSummary:
A set MOE_DAEMON_COMMAND now wins over every resolving daemon script (legacy profile; PROTECTED never reads it), and the override is rewritten so it starts a daemon. MoeDaemonSupervisor gets a `daemonCommandOverride` constructor seam right after processLookup. buildDaemonCommand(basePath, overrideCommand) substitutes {projectPath}, uses a command with --project as written, appends `--project "

"` when a word after the first is a daemon subcommand, and otherwise appends `start --project "

"`, so `npx moe-daemon` becomes `npx moe-daemon start --project "

"`. In WSL agent mode it appends ` --host wsl` unless the command has a --host word. A throwing seam is logged and treated as unset. New MoeDaemonCommandOverrideTest O1-O5, W1/W2 in MoeDaemonSupervisorTest get `{ null }`, and the docs/CONFIGURATION.md row states the precedence and the start rule.
